messages:
ops-bot: INCIDENT DETECTED: sustained p99 token latency spike for hosted inference in us-west-2 starting ~10:02 UTC. error-rate up ~0.6% for gen endpoints. paging oncall.
kevin: @maria i'm oncall, grabbing it. links?
maria: looking at graphs now — p99 jumped from 220ms to ~1.6s for text-gen-main. qps steady, but GPU queues are growing.
sunil: throwing up flame charts — hot spots in kv-cache eviction + small-batch overhead. continuous batching appears to be falling back to small batches for many short requests.
kevin: are there recent deploys? any model swaps?
maria: no deploys in last 30m, last control-plane update 2h ago. infra shows a flurry of large embedding jobs from a handful of orgs at ~09:55 UTC.
sunil: hypothesis: a few long-embedding requests are filling GPU memory, forcing evictions and causing batcher to re-balance -> lots of tiny micro-batches. trade: we can relieve pressure by increasing batch wait (allow larger batches) or by shaping traffic (rate-limit embeddings) or by disabling cross-request KV-cache sharing which is causing frequent evictions.
kevin: want quick mitigations we can do live. priorities: 1) protect latency-sensitive chat routes, 2) reduce OOM/evictions, 3) keep throughput.
tess: I can push config changes to the serving pool. what's the concrete change?
sunil: two simultaneous short mitigations: A) throttle large embedding jobs for non-enterprise orgs by halving their concurrency (quick rate-limit), B) increase continuous batching window and max_batch_tokens to favour throughput (trade p50 up slightly for better p99). Config diffs:
```
# change preview
continuous_batching:
  enabled: true
  mode: aggressive
  max_wait_ms: 50    # was 8
  max_batch_tokens: 12000  # was 4096
route_overrides:
  - route: "/chat/stream"
    latency_sensitive: true
    max_wait_ms: 8
```
# rate-limit API for embeddings for orgs with tier=free
rate_limits:
  embeddings_free_orgs:
    max_concurrency: 2
    window_ms: 1000
```
kevin: good. apply A first (rate-limit embeddings) then B (batching). A should immediately lower memory pressure. Tess, can you apply A as a quick feature flag?
tess: applying rate-limit for embeddings -> pushing config change now. running `curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/configs/apply -d '{"id":"cfg-1845-embed-throttle"}'`
deploy-bot: config apply started: cfg-1845-embed-throttle by tess. target: hosted/us-west-2/pool-a.
prod-observe: config apply success for cfg-1845-embed-throttle. rate-limits active.
maria: memory pressure dropping on GPUs, eviction rate down ~40% vs peak. good.
sunil: ok now push batching change B. note: we keep an explicit override for latency_sensitive routes to preserve interactive UX.
tess: applying batching config: `cfg-1845-batching-v1` -> rolling to pool-a.
deploy-bot: config apply started: cfg-1845-batching-v1 by tess.
kevin: monitoring traces and p99.
prod-observe: config apply success for cfg-1845-batching-v1. continuous_batching.max_wait_ms=50 max_batch_tokens=12000.
maria: immediate effect: throughput +18%, GPU utilization smoother, queue depth higher but fewer tiny batches. p99 dropped from 1.6s -> 520ms within 90s. p50 increased from 220ms -> 320ms for batchable routes.
product-req: flag — some experimental low-latency customers reported UI sluggishness for chat previews. which routes are affected?
sunil: only non-latency-sensitive routes. we left `/chat/stream` override at 8ms. check if customers are hitting non-stream endpoints for interactive paths.
maria: digging. looks like a top-tier customer (org-1729) uses non-stream text-gen for their UX. they saw delay ~100ms additional.
sales-ping: flagged to sales: will notify account leads and offer rollback if they want.
kevin: can we do a per-org override to keep org-1729 at previous batching settings? low overhead.
sunil: yes — add route/org override: `org:1729` -> continuous_batching.max_wait_ms=8. that'll keep them snappy.
tess: applying org override for 1729 now. cfg id cfg-1845-org-1729-override.
deploy-bot: apply success for cfg-1845-org-1729-override.
maria: org-1729 reports latency back to prior levels.
kevin: summary so far: 1) rate-limited large embeddings for free orgs -> immediate mem relief. 2) increased batching window -> throughput up and p99 improved, at cost of higher p50 for some batchable routes. 3) per-org override added for impacted customer.
kevin: any remaining error spikes or OOMs?
maria: error-rate stable ~0.15% above baseline, no new OOMs.
sunil: recommend keeping these changes for now while we monitor for 2h, then iterate with a plan to: a) implement smarter routing to send embedding-heavy requests to dedicated pools, b) implement per-route SLO enforcement so we can automatically keep latency-sensitive routes at small batch windows.
kevin: agree. open follow-up tasks: (1) postmortem + runbook update, (2) alert tuning to include KV eviction rate, (3) product follow-up re: route classification.
tess: creating PR for runbook edits and adding a one-click rollback tag to the config set.
kevin: handing off to next oncall @maria in 20m — keep watch for regressions. key watches: p99, eviction rate, top-10 orgs by GPU tokens/sec. if p99 creeps >800ms re-evaluate.
maria: acknowledged. i'll own monitoring for the window. adding a pinned message with the change IDs and rollback commands.
kevin: thanks team :thumbsup: — incident mitigated for now. will open a brief postmortem doc and label sev-3.
ops-bot: NOTE: if you modified configs during incident, please file a change request in infra-changes with the cfg IDs: cfg-1845-embed-throttle, cfg-1845-batching-v1, cfg-1845-org-1729-override.
kevin: filing CR now. link: https://infra/change/CR-8921
maria: handing off to oncall. next check-in at +60m.
kevin: signing off from this thread. good job.
